rules.title: Direct sanctions exposure
rules.plain: The customer sent crypto to, or received it from, a wallet on the U.S. sanctions list.
next_steps: Freeze or hold per policy and escalate to the sanctions team right away.
Confirm the address matches the OFAC entry character for character.
Check whether other customers have touched the same address.
rules.sql:
-- R01 Direct sanctions exposure
-- A deposit from, or withdrawal to, an address listed on the OFAC SDN list.
-- Any amount alerts: there is no de minimis threshold for sanctions exposure.
SELECT
  'R01' AS rule_id,
  t.customer_id,
  t.tx_id AS anchor_tx_id,
  'critical' AS severity,
  printf('%s of $%,.2f %s a sanctioned wallet (%s, %s)',
         CASE t.direction WHEN 'deposit' THEN 'Deposit' ELSE 'Withdrawal' END,
         t.usd_value,
         CASE t.direction WHEN 'deposit' THEN 'from' ELSE 'to' END,
         s.sdn_name, s.program) AS summary,
  json_object(
    'counterparty', t.counterparty_address,
    'sdn_id', s.sdn_id,
    'sdn_name', s.sdn_name,
    'program', s.program,
    'listed_asset', s.asset
  ) AS evidence
FROM transfers AS t
JOIN sanctioned_addresses AS s ON s.address = t.counterparty_address
-- One alert per transfer even if the address appears under several SDN entries.
GROUP BY t.tx_id;

rules.title: Indirect sanctions exposure (one hop)
rules.plain: The other wallet isn't on the sanctions list, but it has sent or received USDT directly with one that is.
next_steps: Look at who the other wallet is: a big exchange touching many sanctioned wallets means something different from a private wallet dealing with just one.
Open the on-chain link and check the date and amount against the customer's activity.
Ask the customer what the transfer was for if the explanation isn't obvious.
rules.sql:
-- R02 Indirect sanctions exposure (one hop)
-- The counterparty itself is not listed, but it sent USDT to, or received USDT
-- from, a sanctioned address on chain. Exposure is a lead, not a finding: large
-- services (exchanges, bridges) touch many sanctioned addresses, so the alert
-- reports how many distinct sanctioned addresses the counterparty touched and
-- how much it moved, and a reviewer decides whether the link is meaningful.
WITH params AS (
  SELECT 10000.0 AS high_exposure_usdt
),
hop AS (
  SELECT
    CASE WHEN c.from_address = c.sanctioned_address THEN c.to_address ELSE c.from_address END AS address,
    c.sanctioned_address, c.tx_hash, c.amount_usdt, c.block_time
  FROM chain_transfers AS c
),
exposure AS (
  SELECT
    address,
    COUNT(DISTINCT sanctioned_address) AS sanctioned_touched,
    COUNT(*) AS transfers_with_sanctioned,
    SUM(amount_usdt) AS usdt_with_sanctioned,
    MAX(block_time) AS last_seen
  FROM hop
  GROUP BY address
),
largest AS (
  -- The single largest on-chain transfer behind each exposure, cited as evidence.
  SELECT address, tx_hash, sanctioned_address, amount_usdt, block_time,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY address ORDER BY amount_usdt DESC, tx_hash) AS rn
  FROM hop
)
SELECT
  'R02' AS rule_id,
  t.customer_id,
  t.tx_id AS anchor_tx_id,
  CASE WHEN e.usdt_with_sanctioned >= p.high_exposure_usdt THEN 'high' ELSE 'medium' END AS severity,
  printf('%s of $%,.2f %s a wallet that has moved %,.0f USDT with %d sanctioned wallet%s',
         CASE t.direction WHEN 'deposit' THEN 'Deposit' ELSE 'Withdrawal' END,
         t.usd_value,
         CASE t.direction WHEN 'deposit' THEN 'from' ELSE 'to' END,
         e.usdt_with_sanctioned, e.sanctioned_touched,
         CASE e.sanctioned_touched WHEN 1 THEN '' ELSE 's' END) AS summary,
  json_object(
    'counterparty', t.counterparty_address,
    'sanctioned_touched', e.sanctioned_touched,
    'transfers_with_sanctioned', e.transfers_with_sanctioned,
    'usdt_with_sanctioned', round(e.usdt_with_sanctioned, 2),
    'last_seen', e.last_seen,
    'example_tx_hash', l.tx_hash,
    'example_sanctioned_address', l.sanctioned_address,
    'example_amount_usdt', l.amount_usdt,
    'example_block_time', l.block_time
  ) AS evidence
FROM transfers AS t
JOIN exposure AS e ON e.address = t.counterparty_address
JOIN largest AS l ON l.address = e.address AND l.rn = 1
CROSS JOIN params AS p
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sanctioned_addresses AS s WHERE s.address = t.counterparty_address);

rules.title: Pass-through (rapid in and out)
rules.plain: Money came in and most of it went back out within an hour, so the account may just be a stop along the way.
next_steps: Compare against the customer's profile: is fast in-and-out normal for this kind of customer?
Check where the money went next and whether those wallets show up elsewhere.
Ask for the source of funds if the deposit is large for this customer.
rules.sql:
-- R03 Pass-through (rapid in and out)
-- Most of a deposit leaves again within an hour. Funds that only touch the
-- exchange briefly are a common layering step. Expected for some customers
-- (OTC desks, market makers), which is why KYC segment is shown in the alert.
WITH params AS (
  SELECT 60 AS window_minutes, 0.80 AS min_share_out, 50000.0 AS min_deposit_usd
)
SELECT
  'R03' AS rule_id,
  d.customer_id,
  d.tx_id AS anchor_tx_id,
  'medium' AS severity,
  printf('$%,.2f deposit; %.0f%% withdrawn within %d minutes across %d withdrawal%s',
         d.usd_value, 100.0 * SUM(w.usd_value) / d.usd_value, p.window_minutes,
         COUNT(w.tx_id), CASE COUNT(w.tx_id) WHEN 1 THEN '' ELSE 's' END) AS summary,
  json_object(
    'deposit_usd', round(d.usd_value, 2),
    'withdrawn_usd', round(SUM(w.usd_value), 2),
    'minutes_to_last_withdrawal',
      CAST(round((julianday(MAX(w.occurred_at)) - julianday(d.occurred_at)) * 1440) AS INTEGER),
    'withdrawal_tx_ids', json_group_array(w.tx_id)
  ) AS evidence
FROM transfers AS d
CROSS JOIN params AS p
JOIN transfers AS w
  ON w.customer_id = d.customer_id
 AND w.direction = 'withdrawal'
 AND w.occurred_at > d.occurred_at
 AND w.occurred_at <= datetime(d.occurred_at, '+' || p.window_minutes || ' minutes')
WHERE d.direction = 'deposit'
  AND d.usd_value >= p.min_deposit_usd
GROUP BY d.tx_id
HAVING SUM(w.usd_value) >= p.min_share_out * d.usd_value;

rules.title: Structuring below the Travel Rule threshold
rules.plain: Several withdrawals in one day, each just under $3,000, where sender and recipient details become required.
next_steps: Line up the withdrawals by time and amount. Do they look split on purpose?
Check whether the destination wallets belong to the same person.
Collect Travel Rule details for the whole amount and consider a report if splitting is deliberate.
rules.sql:
-- R04 Structuring below the Travel Rule threshold
-- Repeated withdrawals just under $3,000, the U.S. threshold above which
-- originator and beneficiary information must travel with a transmittal
-- (31 CFR 1010.410(f)). Several in one day that add up to a large amount
-- suggest the customer is splitting a transfer to avoid collection.
WITH params AS (
  SELECT 3000.0 AS threshold_usd, 2500.0 AS band_floor_usd,
         4 AS min_count, 10000.0 AS min_total_usd, 24 AS window_hours
),
near AS (
  SELECT t.*
  FROM transfers AS t CROSS JOIN params AS p
  WHERE t.direction = 'withdrawal'
    AND t.usd_value >= p.band_floor_usd AND t.usd_value < p.threshold_usd
),
clusters AS (
  -- Each near-threshold withdrawal opens a window; count what follows within it.
  SELECT a.customer_id, a.tx_id AS anchor_tx_id, a.occurred_at,
         COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(b.usd_value) AS total_usd,
         json_group_array(b.tx_id) AS tx_ids
  FROM near AS a CROSS JOIN params AS p
  JOIN near AS b
    ON b.customer_id = a.customer_id
   AND b.occurred_at >= a.occurred_at
   AND b.occurred_at < datetime(a.occurred_at, '+' || p.window_hours || ' hours')
  GROUP BY a.tx_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= p.min_count AND SUM(b.usd_value) >= p.min_total_usd
),
ranked AS (
  -- Overlapping windows describe the same behavior; keep the largest per customer.
  SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY n DESC, total_usd DESC, occurred_at) AS rn
  FROM clusters
)
SELECT
  'R04' AS rule_id,
  customer_id,
  anchor_tx_id,
  'high' AS severity,
  printf('%d withdrawals between $2,500 and $3,000 within 24 hours, totaling $%,.2f', n, total_usd) AS summary,
  json_object('count', n, 'total_usd', round(total_usd, 2), 'withdrawal_tx_ids', json(tx_ids)) AS evidence
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1;

rules.title: Fan-out to new addresses
rules.plain: One deposit was split and sent to five or more wallets the customer had never paid before.
next_steps: Check whether the customer has a business reason to pay many wallets, like payroll or payouts.
See if the new wallets send money back on to a single place.
Compare the dispersed total to what the customer normally moves.
rules.sql:
-- R05 Fan-out to new addresses (peel / dispersal)
-- One deposit followed within a day by withdrawals to many addresses the
-- customer has never paid before. Dispersal to fresh wallets breaks the trail
-- and is a typical layering step; payroll and payouts look similar, so the
-- alert shows the customer's segment and expected activity.
WITH params AS (
  SELECT 5 AS min_new_addresses, 24 AS window_hours, 0.5 AS min_share_out, 1000.0 AS min_deposit_usd
),
fresh AS (
  -- Withdrawals to an address with no earlier transfer from the same customer.
  SELECT w.*
  FROM transfers AS w
  WHERE w.direction = 'withdrawal'
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM transfers AS prior
      WHERE prior.customer_id = w.customer_id
        AND prior.counterparty_address = w.counterparty_address
        AND prior.occurred_at < w.occurred_at
    )
)
SELECT
  'R05' AS rule_id,
  d.customer_id,
  d.tx_id AS anchor_tx_id,
  'medium' AS severity,
  printf('$%,.2f deposit followed by withdrawals to %d new addresses within %d hours ($%,.2f)',
         d.usd_value, COUNT(DISTINCT f.counterparty_address), p.window_hours, SUM(f.usd_value)) AS summary,
  json_object(
    'deposit_usd', round(d.usd_value, 2),
    'new_addresses', COUNT(DISTINCT f.counterparty_address),
    'dispersed_usd', round(SUM(f.usd_value), 2),
    'withdrawal_tx_ids', json_group_array(f.tx_id)
  ) AS evidence
FROM transfers AS d
CROSS JOIN params AS p
JOIN fresh AS f
  ON f.customer_id = d.customer_id
 AND f.occurred_at > d.occurred_at
 AND f.occurred_at <= datetime(d.occurred_at, '+' || p.window_hours || ' hours')
WHERE d.direction = 'deposit'
  AND d.usd_value >= p.min_deposit_usd
GROUP BY d.tx_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT f.counterparty_address) >= p.min_new_addresses
   AND SUM(f.usd_value) >= p.min_share_out * d.usd_value;

rules.title: Travel Rule information gap
rules.plain: A withdrawal of $3,000 or more went out without the recipient details the Travel Rule requires.
next_steps: Request the missing recipient details before processing more withdrawals.
Check whether this is a one-off or a pattern for the customer.
Treat it as a process fix unless other alerts point to something more.
rules.sql:
-- R06 Travel Rule information gap
-- A withdrawal at or above $3,000 with no beneficiary information recorded.
-- This is a compliance-process alert rather than a suspicion indicator: the
-- fix is usually to collect the information, not to file a report.
WITH params AS (
  SELECT 3000.0 AS threshold_usd
)
SELECT
  'R06' AS rule_id,
  t.customer_id,
  t.tx_id AS anchor_tx_id,
  'low' AS severity,
  printf('$%,.2f withdrawal with no beneficiary information recorded', t.usd_value) AS summary,
  json_object('withdrawal_usd', round(t.usd_value, 2), 'counterparty', t.counterparty_address) AS evidence
FROM transfers AS t
CROSS JOIN params AS p
WHERE t.direction = 'withdrawal'
  AND t.usd_value >= p.threshold_usd
  AND (t.beneficiary_name IS NULL OR trim(t.beneficiary_name) = '');
